name: New in Dubai
about: Just landed? Ask anything about visas, apartments, metro cards, schools and making friends in the city. We were all new once.

stories.author: p07
stories.text: Welcome, newcomers! Metro tip: get your Nol card at the station, not online.

stories.author: p09
stories.text: Apartment hunting tip: check the AC units before you sign. Ask me how I know.

stories.author: p01
stories.text: First weekend in Dubai done. Brunch, a walk, lots of sunscreen. Feeling home.

posts.author: p09
posts.text: Just landed from Toronto with two suitcases and one very confused cat. What are the first three things you wish someone told you about moving here? I'll make a list.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Get a Nol card on day one, and keep the balance topped up. Welcome Hannah!

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Register your pet with the municipality early, it saves a lot of paperwork later.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Buy a fan for the balcony before summer. Trust me, the first heat wave is a shock.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The cat will adjust faster than you, cats are very good at Dubai. Give her time.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Learn the metro routes early, the Red Line is your friend. Welcome to the city!

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Make a bank account early, and keep a copy of your visa paperwork in your phone.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Find a good bakery in the first week. It's the fastest way to feel at home.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee shops are the best community centres. Find one near your flat and be a regular.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Sunscreen before you leave the house, always. The sun here is not a joke in summer.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: @sarak thanks for the note on the bank account. I'm already on the list.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Hannah, also check the water filter at the flat. Tap water is safe but many people filter it.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Welcome to Dubai, the cat will love the AC. Enjoy the best months of the year.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good luck with the move, Hannah. The community here is very friendly, you'll be fine.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Get a local SIM for the data, roaming is expensive and slow in the first weeks.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Learn the basic greetings in Arabic, people love it when newcomers try. Marhaba!

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Join a sports group or a language class, it's the fastest way to make friends here.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Welcome to the group. Come to the next coffee morning, the newcomers always meet there.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Keep the receipts, the paperwork in Dubai has a lot of stamps. Trust me.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swimming at the public beach is a great way to meet locals. Early mornings are best.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Join the Tuesday meetup at the park, it's the biggest newcomer group in town.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks all, the list is already two pages. Going to pin this for the new arrivals.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy says welcome too, he greeted the cat with a very big tail wag.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Yalla Hannah, you've made the right choice. Welcome to Dubai 🌴

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Welcome, Hannah. I'm happy to show you the bike paths when you're settled in.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: The newcomers' run club is on Sunday, you're invited. Bring the cat's blessing, lol.

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Apartment search tip list from my own mistakes: check the water pressure, ask about the chiller bills, and confirm which utilities are included before signing the lease.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Chiller bills! Nobody warns you about that. Ask for last year's average, please.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Check the balcony orientation too. West-facing means the sunset is gorgeous and the heat is brutal.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Water pressure is so important for showers. Turn on every tap before you sign anything.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Read the tenancy contract carefully, the deposit rules and notice periods are in the small print.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A kitchen with a real oven is a deal breaker for a pastry chef. Measure it, really.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Pet-friendly building? Check the rules before you fall in love with the flat.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: The coffee corner in a building is the best sign of a good neighbourhood. Check it out.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Look at the gym and the pool hours too. A good building with good amenities is worth it.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Check the noise levels at night and during the morning rush. Some streets are louder than they seem.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @hannah_b yes, always visit at the same time you'd come home. That's the best test.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Visit twice, once at night and once in the morning. Different city at different hours.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Ask the agent for the building's management contact, it helps when things break.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A written inventory of the flat with photos on move-in day saves your deposit later.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Make sure the internet provider can reach your building before you commit. Some are limited.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thanks, Anjali, this list is gold for newcomers. Printing it for my cousin.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Balcony for the dog and cat, check if it's safe with railings. Important for pets.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Lovely tips. The shade on the balcony matters more than the view, trust the swim coach.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Parking spaces are rare in some buildings. Ask before you sign, it's a real problem.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Shared laundry in some buildings, ask whether it's included or paid per load.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Good point, Yusuf. Some buildings charge for laundry, and that adds up fast.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Also check the air-conditioning maintenance schedule. You don't want a breakdown in August.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Summer breakdown is the worst call in Dubai. Ask the agent for the AC service history.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good list. Save it in your phone so you can tick off each point during the viewing.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Viewing with a checklist is very professional. Bring a torch for the cupboards.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A torch, a tape measure and a calm head. That's the viewing kit for me.

posts.author: p01
posts.text: Got my Emirates ID appointment after three tries online, and the trick was checking the slots at 7am. Hope that saves someone the stress of refreshing all day.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: 7am is the golden hour for appointment slots. Good tip, Sara, thank you.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Bring the original documents and copies, the staff always ask for both.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The waiting area is quieter in the afternoon, I'm told. Pick your time wisely.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Refreshing the page all day is the worst. Set a reminder for 7am, it's easier.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I spent two hours in a queue last week. A tip for the next time: take a number early.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Good luck to everyone, the process is slow but it works. Keep calm and take a snack.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Snack in the bag, always. My last appointment was four hours and I was starving.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Water bottle and a book, the waiting room is a test of patience. Be prepared.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee before the appointment is not allowed, lol, but the vending machine has water.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @hannah_b bring a fully charged phone, the queue number app is handy.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Copies of everything in one folder, in the same order as the form. Makes the staff happy.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Organise the documents in clear plastic sleeves. Little details like that help a lot.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy doesn't need an ID, but he has a microchip. Very easy life, honestly.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks for the tip, Sara. I'll check at 7am tomorrow for my renewal.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Renewal reminders should be on the phone calendar, at least a month before expiry.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: A month before the expiry is a smart rule. Don't wait until the last week.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll make a checklist for the next newcomer appointment. Anyone want a copy?

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Yes please, the checklist would be useful for the swimmers' visa too.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Keep the checklist short. Long lists scare people more than the queue does.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good point, Yusuf. Five items, big font, one page. Simple.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Sara, you're the hero of this week. The 7am trick is very useful for everyone.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Thanks for sharing your experience. It's exactly the kind of post this group needs.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Congrats on the ID! The first step is the hardest, now enjoy the city.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Congratulations, Sara! Next: the bank account, and then the coffee tour.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy celebrates your ID with a happy bark. He is very proud of the newcomers.

posts.author: p05
posts.text: Best places to meet other dog owners in the city if you just moved here with a puppy? Feeling lonely and the puppy wants to play with everything.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: The Marina walk is full of dog owners in the morning. Say hi, that's how it starts.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Mushrif park on Saturdays, the pet parents group meets there. Everyone is welcoming.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Puppy classes are a great way to meet owners. Ask your vet for a recommendation.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Running with a dog is a good way to make friends at dawn, the early birds are friendly.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Join the Pet Parents group, Mariam runs great meetups. Very welcoming for newcomers.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: The cafe with the dog bowl in Mirdif is a good meeting point. The baristas are lovely.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Puppy playdates are the best. Start small and let the pups decide the pace.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Lonely in a new city is so real. Coffee mornings and pet meetups are the cure.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee shops with a community table are amazing for meeting people. Ask for the big table.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: @hannah_b thank you, everyone. I'll go to the Mushrif meetup this Saturday with the puppy.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good plan. Bring water for the pup, the park gets warm quickly after eight.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Look out for the friendly golden retriever there, he's the unofficial greeter.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Marina dog walkers are very social on Friday evenings too. Good for newcomers.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Add a dog park visit in the summer evening, shaded lanes, and a lot of happy dogs.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Puppy will have a lot of friends by the end of the month, I predict it.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Lonely feelings pass with time. Keep putting yourself out there, Mariam. You've got this.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Puppy's first friend in Dubai should be a cat, obviously. Call Anjali, she has Mango.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Mango is available for playdates, but she is strict about the rules. Heh.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Dog and cat playdates are the hottest social events in the city this season.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Let the puppy make friends at his own pace, and you'll make friends too.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Welcome to Dubai, Mariam. The community is kind, and the puppy will be the star.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: See you on the Marina walk at dawn, I'll bring the puppy's favourite treat.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dog people are the best people. Good luck settling in, Mariam.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let me know how the Saturday meetup goes. Pictures please, the puppy deserves them.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Yalla, new friends and new routines. Welcome to the city, habibti 🐾

posts.author: p02
posts.text: Newcomer question: how do you find a good doctor in Dubai? Do I need insurance first or can I just walk into a clinic and pay? Trying to understand the basics.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Insurance first, always. Check which clinics are in your network before you need one.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Clinics do take cash and card, but insurance makes it much cheaper. Ask at reception.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Ask neighbours and colleagues for a GP recommendation. Word of mouth beats the directories.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: A family doctor near home is the best starting point. Book a check-up in the first month.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our office insurance covers a network of clinics, the HR team shared the list. Ask your employer.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Take the insurance card to every visit. The receptionists are very strict about it.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ask your doctor for a written summary after each visit, it helps when you move or switch.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Pharmacies have many common medicines without a prescription, but check the label first.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Keep a list of allergies and past medicines on your phone. Good habit for any new city.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks all, this is exactly what I needed. Insurance card goes in the wallet today.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: @ravi_menon also check if the clinic has a pharmacy inside, it saves a trip.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Sports injuries in Dubai are common, so a sports physio on your list is a smart idea.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Ask about a second opinion policy, some insurers need a referral for specialists.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Referral rules are the part that surprised me most. Read the policy carefully.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Keep your health records in one place too, digital copies are easiest.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Emergency numbers saved in the phone, and the nearest hospital on the map. Basic but vital.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: The emergency number is 999 for ambulance, saving that one today. Stay safe everyone.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Good call, Layla. Add the non-emergency clinic number too, it's useful for weekends.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thanks everyone. Doctor search is on my list for this weekend.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's vet is great, I'm happy to recommend one for the newcomers too.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good luck, Ravi. Settling in takes time, be kind to yourself.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: This thread is super useful. Pin it for the next newcomer, please.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Pinned by the group admin? Let me ask, otherwise I'll do it myself. Yalla.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Great community spirit. Everyone helps the next newcomer, that's Dubai at its best.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thank you all, I feel much more prepared now. The city is starting to feel friendly.

posts.author: p03

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Manakish for breakfast is my new ritual. Thank you, Layla, I'm going tomorrow.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Lebanese bakeries are the heart of this city. The za'atar is always fresh.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Sourdough behind a supermarket is the most Dubai secret ever. Keep sharing.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy requested a sample but I told him the manakish is for humans only, sorry.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: My favourite local find is a shawarma place in Deira with the best garlic sauce.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: The bakery near the running track has amazing date bread. Perfect for a post-run snack.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Local finds are my favourite part of the city. Adding this bakery to the newcomer list.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Kwame's favourite find is a jazz cafe in Al Quoz. Live music on Thursdays, very cool.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A late breakfast at the Lebanese bakery after my swim is the best routine ever.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Thanks all, the sourdough is getting a fan club. Let's do a bakery crawl next month.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Bakery crawl is brilliant. Add a coffee stop between each one, it's the law.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Yes! Bakery crawl with the newcomers, that's a great way to meet people.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I'll make the map for the bakery crawl. Send me your favourite spots.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Please include the one near the metro, it has the best croissants in the area.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: A croissant at the metro bakery, the perfect commuter snack. Adding it.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Map plus snack plus friends, the perfect Saturday for a newcomer like me.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is now officially invited to the bakery crawl, as long as the dog bowl is there.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dog-friendly bakery stop, yes. Please bring a bowl, puppy has earned it.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Bakery crawl on a Friday morning, I'll bring my appetite and a notebook for the recs.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: The notebook is a great idea, Kwame. We should make a little recipe guide too.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Recipe guide with coffee pairings. My dream project, honestly.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Layla, your bakery finds are the reason I'm getting out of the flat more. Thank you.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The map is ready soon. I'll post it in the group, no external links here.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Yalla, bakery crawl next month, I'm in. Sourdough and friends 🥖

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Brilliant spirit in this thread. I love how the newcomers are helping each other.

posts.author: p06
posts.text: Salik tags: I got charged for a toll I didn't know I passed. Is there a simple way to check my account and set up a top up? Trying to avoid surprises at month end.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Check your account in the official app or the portal, it lists every crossing with the time and place.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Set a low-balance alert if the option is available. It's easier than checking every month.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Many newcomers get caught by the toll gates on the highway. Keep an eye on the rental car.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Rental car tolls are charged to the company, then they bill you later. Ask the agency.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: I'd keep a small balance in the tag account, just a habit that helps.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's trips in the car are free, but the tolls are not. Sadly that is life.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Ask your landlord if the car park is included. Parking charges can be a surprise too.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I read the statement every month, it's boring but it saves money.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks Kwame, I'll check the official portal tonight and set the alert.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: @hannah_b good plan. Save the link in your phone so you don't have to search for it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Official portal only, never trust random links. The scam messages are getting clever.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good warning. Always check the official site address before you enter any details.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A quick check of the tag balance each week is a nice habit. Good luck, Kwame.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Tolls are fair in exchange for fast roads. Plan the trip and the budget together.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee budget and toll budget, the two line items that keep me honest.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Thanks for the warning about the messages. Puppy is safer than I thought, lol.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: This is a good thread for newcomers. Keep the tips coming, friends 🙌

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Also consider a car-free plan, the metro and taxis are good in the city centre.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Metro plus a bike is my plan for the summer. Fewer tolls, more sunshine.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Thanks, everyone. Off to check the account now, and then a long coffee.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck, Kwame. Tolls are a small price for a city this fast.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Remember the official app, and check the statement once a month. You've got this 🙂

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Keep the toll tags stuck on the windscreen the right way, that's a common mistake.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Ask a friend to check the account with you the first time, it's less stressful.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Save the official app on the home screen so you don't have to search for it.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Winter is coming to Dubai soon and I'm told the evenings are perfect for walks. Which neighbourhood has the best outdoor spaces for a new arrival who wants to explore?

comments.author: p01
comments.text: The Marina walk is lovely in winter, cool breeze and sunsets. Also Jumeirah beach at night.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Al Quoz has the best art walks in the cooler months. The murals are worth a slow walk.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Jumeirah beach at sunset is a must. The sea breeze in winter is refreshing.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Running trails by the lake in JLT are good in winter, the air is crisp and clear.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Mirdif has big parks with shaded paths. Perfect for weekend picnics and dog walks.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Downtown has the lake promenade with the fountains. Winter nights there are magical.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Downtown is so pretty at night, and the bakeries are open late. Dangerous, but worth it.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Business Bay has a canal walk with cafes, very good for a quiet evening after work.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves any park with a long grass patch. Mirdif is his winter favourite.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @anjali_rao thanks for Mirdif, that's on the list. Explore everything.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dress in layers, the evenings can be cooler than you expect near the water.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Also bring a light jacket. The sea wind in winter feels colder than the thermometer.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee and a walk, the perfect winter ritual. Please make the most of the season.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Winter runs are the best of the year, honest. Dress warm and enjoy the lake.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Dubai winters are short and sweet. Plan a few outdoor brunches before the heat returns.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Winter is the season of picnics and rooftop nights, so enjoy the cool air.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Picnic with a cake and a flask of coffee on the grass. My dream winter weekend.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Winter in Dubai is the season I love most. Everyone's outside, the city feels alive.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Good luck Tomasz, and welcome to the best season in the city. Puppy is very excited.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim season is still open in winter for the brave. Try it once, you'll be hooked.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Winter sunsets over the Marina are the best free show in the city. Don't miss them.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks everyone, this is a great list. I'll try a different neighbourhood each weekend.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A different neighbourhood each weekend, the best way to know a city. Yalla 🌅

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Make sure to tell us what you liked. The group loves a good neighbourhood review.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: I will. Thanks for the warm welcome, everyone. Dubai is already feeling like home.
